extracted.intended_audience: general readers and film enthusiasts seeking encyclopedic information about the film
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing and documenting the production, release, reception, influence, and controversies of a single feature film (Breakfast at Tiffany's). Useful for readers assessing a film's commercial, critical, cultural, and historical standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box office / commercial success
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of the film's commercial performance: the article reports Breakfast at Tiffany's grossed $14 million worldwide on a $2.5 million budget and notes theatrical release and specific screenings (e.g., Radio City Music Hall).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gross vs. budget, theater engagements and contemporary trade coverage (Variety) to assess commercial success; the page cites specific figures and trade notices calling it 'a bright box office contender.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical response / reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporary and retrospective critical reception: aggregator scores (Rotten Tomatoes: 87% of 100 critics; Metacritic: 77/100) and selected critic quotes (Time, The New York Times, Chicago Tribune, Philadelphia Inquirer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate using aggregate scores, consensus statements, and notable individual reviews; the article includes both praise (Hepburn's performance, screenplay, supporting cast) and critical observations (anachronisms, deviations from the novella).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and accolades
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition by major institutions: nominated for five Academy Awards (won two: Music Score and Best Song), Grammy nominations/wins, Writers Guild win, AFI rankings, National Film Registry induction, and various international awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count nominations and wins across relevant awards (Oscars, Grammys, WGA, Golden Globes, AFI lists) and note registry inductions to gauge artistic and institutional recognition; the article lists specific awards and placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance / acting (Audrey Hepburn and supporting cast)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of performances: Hepburn's portrayal garnered widespread critical acclaim and a Best Actress nomination; supporting performances (Peppard, Ebsen, Balsam) are singled out positively while Rooney's is criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge lead and supporting performances by contemporary reviews, nominations, and later critical reassessment; the page emphasizes Hepburn's role as iconic and influential on her career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music and song ('Moon River')
rubrics_metrics.description: The film's music scored by Henry Mancini, with the song 'Moon River' (lyrics by Johnny Mercer) tailored to Hepburn, receiving major awards (Best Song) and critical attention to arrangement and placement in the film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess soundtrack impact via awards, composer/lyricist credits, contemporary reaction (Time's notes on arrangement), and how the music functions in the film; the article details composition anecdotes and award outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation fidelity / screenplay changes from the novella
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which the screenplay deviates from Truman Capote's novella: changes include converting the unnamed gay narrator to a heterosexual male lead, altering tone toward romantic comedy, adding and expanding characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider faithfulness to source material, notable plot/character changes, and author reaction (Capote disliked the adaptation); the article documents the screenplay's departures and resulting controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting and development choices
rubrics_metrics.description: History of casting and production decisions: many actors were considered for roles, the original director (John Frankenheimer) was replaced by Blake Edwards, and screenplay writers were exchanged during development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how casting selection, director changes, and screenwriter replacements shaped the finished film; the article lists considered actors (Monroe, MacLaine, McQueen, Lemmon, etc.) and production rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting controversy / problematic portrayals (I. Y. Yunioshi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical controversy over Mickey Rooney's portrayal of I. Y. Yunioshi, described as a caricature of a Japanese man, labeled racist by later commentators and protested by Asian-American groups; producers and director later expressed regret or defended choices in different accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat depiction of ethnic/racial characters as a serious evaluative criterion: note makeup/prosthetics, casting choices, contemporary publicity deception, later apologies, and audience/protester responses; the article details examples and reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural influence and iconic imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: The film's impact on popular culture and fashion: Hepburn's image (high chignon, cigarette holder), the Givenchy black dress (described as 'the most famous little black dress'), sunglasses re-releases, and influence on later visual designs (e.g., Catwoman illustrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess long-term cultural footprint via iconic stills, fashion influence, auctions (dress sale prices), reissues of merchandise, and references in other media; the article cites specific examples and sources (Glamour, Christie's).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and historical significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Official recognition of historical/cultural importance: the film was preserved in the U.S. National Film Registry by the Library of Congress (2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use registry inclusion and similar preservation actions as measures of lasting historical importance; the page mentions the National Film Registry induction explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production quality and filmmaking craftsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical and production credits and on-set details: director Blake Edwards, cinematography by Franz F. Planer, editing by Howard Smith, filming locations (New York City exteriors, Paramount Studios interiors), and production anecdotes (difficulties during opening sequence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate direction, cinematography, editing, location work and production anecdotes to judge filmmaking craft; the article provides credits and specific filming stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home media releases and restorations
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and preservation through home media: VHS (1989), DVD (2001), anniversary special editions with featurettes (2006, 2009), and a 50th-anniversary Blu-ray digital restoration (2011).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider quality of restorations, bonus materials, and continued availability as indicators of cultural relevance and scholarly/accessibility value; the page lists editions and restoration details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence on careers
rubrics_metrics.description: The film's role in the professional trajectories of cast and crew: e.g., helped rejuvenate Buddy Ebsen's career and is cited as influential in Hepburn's later roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how a film affected the subsequent careers of key contributors via contemporary reporting and later commentary; the article cites examples and critical commentary on career impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reception over time / changing perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolving critical and public interpretations: initial acclaim (performance, music, style) contrasted with later criticisms (racial caricature, fidelity to Capote); the article documents both contemporary praise and retrospective reassessments and protests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for shifts in cultural norms and critical frameworks when judging a film: compare original reviews and awards with later controversies, protests, and scholarly reassessments as the article does.
